title: Exam questions self-mark ignores the M1/A1 codes on Maths worked-derived items, and the Answer line counts as a mark
detail: 592 of the 1,244 Maths exam parts (48%) are derived from exam-style worked examples by KOS.content.examFromWorked. Each mark-scheme point is one STEP, ending in its codes, for example '[M1 A1]', and the worked answer is added as an extra point, '**Answer:** …'. The self-mark tally in js/engines/quiz.js knows nothing about those codes. When the number of points equals the marks (106 parts), each tick counts as 1 mark. When there are more points (112 parts), it caps at the total. When there are fewer (374 parts), it scales the marks in proportion. Repro on maths 1.1 Q1 (3 marks; points '[M1 A1]', '[A1]', 'Answer'): ticking only the Answer line awards 1/3, and ticking only the [M1 A1] step also awards 1/3, when it is worth 2. Each row prints '1' beside it. The needsM rule (an A needs its M) never applies, because the lines start with the working, not with 'A1'. So the logged exam session (KOS.sessions.log type exam, marks/max) records partial marks that do not match the mark scheme it shows. The 652 bank parts are written one point per mark and are correct.
evidence: shots/content-maths/selfmark-answerline-mac.png (Answer ticked → Awarded 1/3; step 1 shows [M1 A1] but '1'); eval on #/ref/maths/1.1 Exam questions: onlyAnswerTicked '1', onlyStep1Ticked '1'; counts via eval over KOS_CONTENT: derived parts 592 (perMark 106, more 112, fewer 374), bank 652 all perMark; js/core/content.js:547-555 (ms = one line per step + '[mk]', Answer pushed as a point); js/engines/quiz.js:264-268 (needsM tests /^\s*A\d/), :286-296 (perMark / proportional fromTicks)
rootCause: examFromWorked emits one scheme point per step (several marks) plus the answer, but the tally assumes one point = one mark or scales proportionally
fix: In examFromWorked, expand each step into one point per mark code (e.g. '[M1] …', '[A1] …' with the step text on the first), so the scheme is one point per mark like the banks; do not push the Answer as a point (show it as a separate 'Answer' line under the scheme). Alternatively give points a weight parsed from their [codes] and make fromTicks sum weights and needsM read the code tokens. Add a smoke check: Σ point weights = marks for every exam part.

title: 24 exam-style worked examples carry mark codes that do not add up to their stated marks
detail: An exam-style worked example states its total in src (e.g. '· 11 marks'), and each step carries its Edexcel codes (mk). In 24 of the 604 Maths exam-tagged examples, the codes add up to a different total. Examples: 5.9 'Tide model' is stated as 11 marks, but its codes (B1 M1 A1 · B1 · B1 · M1 A1 A1) add up to 8. 3.4 'The dam' is stated as 11, with codes adding up to 8. 8.3 'Equal areas either side of the axis' is stated as 10, with codes adding up to 8. 5.1 'Badge' is stated as 4, with codes adding up to 5. 2.3 'Complete the square, sketch…' is stated as 10, with codes adding up to 11. A learner reading the model answer cannot tell where the missing marks come from, or why there are extra ones, and the derived exam item (marks = src) inherits the inconsistency. Full list: 2.3×2, 2.6, 2.7×2, 2.8, 3.2, 3.4×2, 4.1×2, 5.1, 5.7, 5.9×2, 6.6×2, 7.6, 8.3×2, 8.5, 8.7, S2.4, S4.2.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/mk2.js output (24 rows: leaf | title | stated | sum of step codes); e.g. node cm/mk.js 'Tide model' → mks ["B1 M1 A1","B1","B1","M1 A1 A1"] vs src 'A-level Specimen · P1 Q13 · 11 marks'
rootCause: Hand-authored mk codes, with no check that their sum equals the src mark count (smoke65/66 hold CS to a depth contract; Maths has no equivalent mark-sum lint)
fix: Correct each of the 24 from the published mark scheme: add the missing codes or fix the total. Add a lint (in the Maths smoke) that the sum of the codes equals the src marks for every exam-tagged worked example.

title: A worked example citing two questions becomes a 4-mark exam item whose scheme covers 7 marks
detail: 7.1 'Prove d/dx(x^3) = 3x^2; and y = 2x^2' has src 'AS June 2018 · P1 Q10 · 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4 · 3 marks'. examFromWorked takes only the FIRST 'N marks' (/(\d+)\s*marks?/.exec). The resulting exam item is marked 4 marks and labelled AS, but its question has parts (i) and (ii) worth 7. Its src string also keeps '· 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4', because only a trailing '· N marks' is stripped.
evidence: eval: KOS_CONTENT['maths:7.1'].exam item → {marks:4, src:'Edexcel June 2018 · P1 Q10 · 4 marks; A-level June 2022 · P2 Q4', level:'AS'}; js/core/content.js:542-546
fix: Either split the worked example into two cards (one per question), or have examFromWorked sum every 'N marks' in src and strip each. The first is cleaner.

title: Newton–Raphson generator prints a 'Root estimate' that is not a root in about a third of its random examples
detail: The worked-example generator 'newraph', wired to 9.3, always does exactly three iterations from a random x0 and then prints 'Root estimate: x ≈ …', whatever f is at that point. In 138 of 400 random examples, |f(x3)| > 0.01. Two cases: x^3 − 2x − 5 from x0 = 1 gives 'x ≈ 3.34870 (f ≈ 25.85)' (the true root is 2.0946), and x^3 + x − 1 from x0 = 3 gives 'x ≈ 0.88069 (f ≈ 0.564)' (the true root is 0.6823). A learner using the generator to check their own working is taught that a non-converged value is the answer.
evidence: eval on slot 7: 400 runs of KOS.worked.byIds(['newraph'])[0] → bad 138; examples quoted above; js/labs/worked.js:704 (Root estimate step printed unconditionally after three iterations)
fix: Iterate until |x_{n+1} − x_n| < 1e-6 (cap about 20) and show the first three steps plus 'converges to …'. Or pick x0 near a root (from a sign change). If it does not converge, say so ('not converged yet: f(x3) = …').

title: Normal-distribution generator writes the symmetric interval backwards, e.g. P(61 < X < 51)
detail: When the random x is below μ (89 of 200 runs), the 'Complements you might need' step prints P(2μ − x < X < x). Example: X ~ N(56, 2²), x = 51 gives 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876'. That is an empty interval written as if it were the answer.
evidence: eval on slot 7: normal solve with {mu:56,sg:2,x:51} → 'P(61 < X < 51) = 0.9876 (symmetric interval about μ)'; js/labs/worked.js:549

title: Hypothesis-test generators draw contradictory set-ups (testing p < p0 with x far above the mean)
detail: The 'hyptest' generator (S5.2) draws the tail and x independently. In 187 of 400 random examples, x lies on the wrong side of the mean for the alternative being tested. Example: H1: p < 0.4 with n = 17 and x = 15 gives P(X ≤ 15) = 1.00000. The example is formally right but teaches nothing, and no exam question is set up that way. The projectile generator also prints '−0 = 20T − 4.9T²' and '4.9T² − 20T − 0 = 0' whenever h = 0 (174 of 400 runs). The partial-fractions and normal-parameters generators print unbracketed double signs: '(5·-1 + -1) / (-1 − 1)' and 'μ = 25 − -0.9945 × 8.0963'.
evidence: eval on slot 7 (400-run sweeps of every one of the 36 Maths generators: no exceptions or NaN; hyptestSilly 187/400; projectile '−0' 174/400); js/labs/worked.js:752 (hyptest random); js/labs/worked-extra.js:356-373 (projectile)
fix: hyptest: draw x from the alternative's side (below n·p0 for 'lower'), and draw h in the projectile generator only when h > 0 or drop the term. Use a shared signed formatter that brackets negatives inside a product or after a minus sign.

title: Seven Maths callouts use an undefined kind 'key' and render as an unlabelled teal Tip
detail: The callout schema (js/core/content.js:31, CALLOUT_META :49-58) knows info, def, tip, warn, miscon, mnemonic, memorise and formula. Seven Maths callouts in 1.1, 9.2, 9.3 and 10.x use t:'key'. The renderer falls back to the Tip icon (◆), and the stylesheet has no [data-kind=key] rule, so they get the base teal, the same as info and formula. The author meant a 'key idea' box, but on the page it cannot be told apart from an ordinary formula or info box.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/beh1.js output 'bad callout types: key 7'; grep -rn 't: "key"' js/data/content → maths-pure-p1.js:152, maths-pure-p10.js:27, :437 and maths-pure-p9.js; js/core/content.js:346 (CALLOUT_META[t] || tip); css/views/study.css:321-334 (no key rule)
fix: Either add a 'key' kind to CALLOUT_META and the stylesheet (e.g. 'Key idea', crimson), or change the seven to an existing kind. Then make validate_content.js reject unknown callout kinds.

title: Two bank items depend on the item before them and break when the quiz is shuffled (M8.4 'Tension then:')
detail: The M8.4 bank item Q6 reads only 'Tension then:' (options 0 / 39.2 N / 78.4 N / 19.6 N). It relies on Q5 ('Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley'). The quiz has a Shuffle control that reorders the questions (js/engines/quiz.js:66), so after a shuffle, or when Q6 appears alone in a review of missed items, the question has no data. A sweep of all 1,058 Maths quiz stems found no other stem that leans on the previous item: the 'then' in 4.1, M7.1 and M9.1 completes the sentence.
evidence: js/data/content/bank-maths-mech.js (M8.4 quiz, items 5–6); node print of maths:M8.4 quiz: 'Q5b Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. Acceleration: … Q6b Tension then:'; stem-dependency regex sweep over KOS_CONTENT maths quiz
fix: Make Q6 self-contained: 'Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. The tension is:'.

title: 6.4 flashcard question mixes base 2 and base 10 in one garbled stem
detail: The 6.4 bank card reads 'Solve log_2(x+3) + log_2(x+10) = 2 + 2log_2 x… with base 10 and 2 = log 100.' The answer works in base 10 ((x+3)(x+10) = 100x², x = 0.620), so the stem is a half-edited sentence. Read as written (base 2), the answer would be (x+3)(x+10) = 4x², giving x = 6, which is a different answer.
fix: Rewrite the stem as 'Solve log(x+3) + log(x+10) = 2 + 2 log x (base 10).'

title: 'Retry the N missed' overwrites the topic's quiz score with the retry's: 9/13 then 4/4 records lastPct 100 and the head reads 'best 9/4'
detail: After a quiz, 'Retry the N missed' (js/engines/quiz.js:178-181) mounts the SAME engine on the missed subset with the topic's own stats record. finish() (quiz.js:156-160) then sets lastPct = correct / subset size, logs a second 'quiz' session with total = the subset, and the head line compares the stored best (a count out of the full quiz) with the subset length. Repro on #/ref/maths/M7.3 (empty account): answer every question with A → 9/13, record {attempts 1, best 9, lastPct 69}; press 'Retry the 4 missed', answer them right → record {attempts 2, best 9, lastPct 100}, sessions [{9/13 69%}, {4/4 100%}], head 'score 4 · best 9/4'. RAG reads lastPct (js/modules/rag.js:63-71), so a learner who got 69% now shows no quiz weakness at all, and the ledger/Reports count a 100% quiz that never happened.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/qz-retry.js (eval on slot 7, output quoted); shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png ('best 9/13', inspector 'Quiz attempts 2', 'Data says Green'); js/engines/quiz.js:156-165, :178-181; js/modules/rag.js:63-71
fix: Pass a 'practice' flag for the missed retry: do not touch st.lastPct/best (or record it under a separate missedRetry field), log it as a practice session (or not at all), and print the head as 'retrying 4 missed' instead of best/total.
rootCause: The missed-retry reuses mountMCQ's normal finish path, which assumes items is the topic's whole quiz.

title: One mediocre quiz makes a Maths topic 'Data says Green': the RAG starts at 100 and a 69% quiz only takes 8 points off
detail: rag.auto (js/modules/rag.js:30-110) starts every topic at score 100 and SUBTRACTS for weak signals; band() (rag.js:17) is Green from 70. With only a quiz as evidence, the most a quiz can remove is 25 (lastPct 0 %), so ANY single quiz attempt — even 0 % — leaves the topic Amber or Green, and a 69 % quiz removes 8 → Green. Thin evidence (one quiz, no cards rated, no exam questions, 0/4 checks, status Not started) is judged as mastery. Repro: empty account, M7.3, quiz answered all-A (9/13 = 69 %): inspector shows 'Data says Green' beside 'Not started' and '0/4 checks'. The answer-position bias (all-A scores 69 %) makes this reachable without reading a single question.
evidence: shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png; js/modules/rag.js:17 (band), :63-71 (quiz penalty capped at 25), :103 (no minimum evidence); eval qz-retry.js before the retry: lastPct 69 → band g
fix: Make the auto band evidence-weighted: start from 'no claim' and require a minimum amount of evidence (e.g. ≥ N cards rated or a quiz ≥ 80 % plus another signal) before Green; map a lone quiz to a score proportional to its percentage rather than a capped deduction.
rootCause: Subtractive scoring from 100 with capped penalties and no evidence threshold.

title: Long worked-step lines push the topic page sideways on iPhone: 14 lines in 9 Maths leaves run up to 114px past the screen
devices: iPhone (402px); not on iPad 820 or Mac
detail: Worked-example steps are written as inline $\displaystyle …$ maths, so KaTeX renders them as a .katex span, not a .katex-display (whose overflow-x: auto in css/base.css:153 would make it scroll). The step body .k-n-wm (css/views/study.css:356 .k-n-wbody, no overflow rule) lets the line run on, and on iPhone the step column is only 177px wide (the 'Step' label column takes the rest). The over-wide line widens <main> (scrollWidth 516 vs 402 on S2.1), so the whole topic page can be panned sideways; panned, the step labels leave the screen and the maths bleeds past the card edge. Sweep of all 433 Maths note pages at 402px: 14 lines in 4.1 (4), 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4 (2), 8.3, 8.7, 9.2, S2.1 (2), overflowing by 7-114px. iPad portrait: none.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/ovf.js → cm/ovf-iphone.json (433 pages, 14 katex lines offscreen), cm/ovf-ipad.json (0); shots/content-maths/top-s21-clip-iphone.png (S2.1 page 4 after the page was panned to the σ line: labels gone, line runs past the card); eval: main.scrollWidth 516 / clientWidth 402 on #/ref/maths/S2.1; js/core/content.js:382 (.k-n-wm wraps para(st.m)); css/views/study.css:351-356
fix: Give .k-n-wm (and other step/answer bodies) overflow-x: auto with the same tab-stop-when-scrolls rule as tables, or render a step whose maths is wider than its column as a display block; on phones stack the Step label above the body to give the maths the full width.
rootCause: Inline \displaystyle maths in a grid cell with no horizontal scroller.

title: On iPhone the Maths plot labs draw their axis numbers at 5.7px (half the 11px label floor)
detail: Every plot lab (lab.plot) writes tick and curve labels at size 14 in the 800-unit viewBox (js/labs/lab.js:252 Math.max(14,…), :317, :321, :325, :382). On iPhone the stage is 326px wide, so the drawing is scaled ×0.41 and every label renders at 5.7 CSS px; the phone crop (lab.js:455-476) does not help a plot because the plot frame fills the viewBox. Measured with getScreenCTM on the Simulations tab: 9.3 Newton–Raphson 16 labels at 5.7px, 9.4 Trapezium rule 21, M7.5 projectiles 18, S4.2 Normal 15, 7.1 21, M9.1 8 at 6.6–7.1px, 10.3 24 at 10.4px. CLAUDE.md invariant 63 sets an 11px label floor for charts. The axis numbers in the screenshot cannot be read without zooming.
evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/simtxt.js (iphone/ipad/mac output quoted above); shots/content-maths/top-sim-9-4-iphone.png (dpr 2); shots/content-maths/sim-9-3-iphone.png; js/labs/lab.js:252, :317-326, :481 (lab.narrow)
fix: Scale label size by the stage's px-per-unit (size = 11px / scale, capped) or switch plots to a narrower viewBox when lab.narrow() is true (as the floating-point and subnetting labs do), and thin the ticks (every other tick) so the bigger labels do not collide.
rootCause: Label sizes are fixed in viewBox units, so they shrink with the stage.

title: A third of Maths quiz explanations are a bare label: 352 of 1,058 'why' lines are three words or fewer with no working ('Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Add.', 'Tables.')
detail: After a wrong answer the quiz shows the item's 'why' as the explanation. In 352 of 1,058 Maths quiz items (99 base, 253 bank) it is three words or fewer with no maths: 'Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Power law.' ×5, 'Product rule.', 'Multiply.', 'Add.', 'Tables.', 'Vertex.', 'Union.', 'Conjugate.'. A learner who picked the wrong option is told the name of a rule, not why their option was wrong or what the right working is. The bank files are the main source (253 of 560 bank items vs 99 of 498 base).
evidence: node one-liner over cm/load.js (KOS_CONTENT maths quiz): 352/1058 label-only, by source {base 99, bank 253}; examples: maths:2.2 Q11 'Conjugate.', maths:2.3 Q14 'Vertex.', maths:2.5 Q10 'Union.'; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js
fix: Rewrite the label-only whys as one line of working that names the misconception behind the most tempting wrong option (e.g. 'Multiply by the conjugate $3-\sqrt7$, so the denominator becomes $9-7=2$').
rootCause: Bank items were authored with terse whys and no length/quality check in validate_content.

title: Four Pure leaf titles show raw caret notation ('e^x', 'Gradient of e^kx', 'Solving a^x = b', 'Differentiating x^n, e^kx…') in the spine, heading and search
detail: The SHORT title table in tools/gen_data.py writes four titles in ASCII maths: 6.1 'Exponential functions & e^x', 6.2 'Gradient of e^kx', 6.5 'Solving a^x = b', 7.2 'Differentiating x^n, e^kx, trig, ln x'. Titles are plain text (the spine, the page h1, breadcrumbs, search results, Reports and the Assistant all print them as-is), so the learner sees literal carets in an otherwise typeset subject.
evidence: shots/content-maths/top-51-fig-azure-ipadl.png (spine: 'Exponential functions & e^x', 'Gradient of e^kx', 'Solving a^x = b'); tools/gen_data.py SHORT entries 6.1, 6.2, 6.5, 7.2; js/data/maths.js:521
fix: Use Unicode superscripts in the titles (eˣ, eᵏˣ, aˣ, xⁿ) in the SHORT table and regenerate js/data/maths.js with --format-existing.
rootCause: Generated titles are plain strings written with ASCII exponents.
